Hence the same weight on the pan for the blocks in the two cases indicates that the limiting friction is independent of the surface area. 4.9 Angle of Friction: It is the angle made by the resultant of the normal reaction and the frictional force with the normal reaction. In the fig, θ is the angle of friction.
Fig 4.11: Showing angle of friction and angle of repose Physics, Grade 11 | 94

Let R = mg represent the normal reaction to a block of mass m, and let F be the frictional force opposing the motion. Therefore, OC = Res represents the resultant of R and F, making an angle θ with the vertical. By definition, θ is the angle of friction. Now, from the fig 4.12; Tanθ = RC = F = μ OA R i.e, the tangent of the angle of friction is equal to the coefficient of the friction. 4.10 Angle of Repose The angle of inclination that a solid kept on the inclined plane just begins to slide down is called the angle of repose.

Fig 4.12: Showing angle of repose In the fig, mg is the weight of the block of mass m placed on an inclined plane to which R is the normal reaction. The normal reaction R is balanced by the component mgcosθ, while the component mgsinθ down the inclined plane contributes to the block sliding down, which is balanced by the upward-directed frictional force F. Therefore, we writeF = mgsinθ R = mgcosθ ⟹ F = tanθ R ∴ tanθ =μ i.e. the tangent of the angle of repose is equal to the coefficient of friction. Moreover, from the study of the angle of friction and angle of repose, it is found that; Angle of friction = angle of repose i.e., α =θ.
